newsitem.title: CONGO: Former Congo military ruler ends 17-month absence.
newsitem.headline: Former Congo military ruler ends 17-month absence.

text.p: Congo's former Marxist military ruler Denis Sassou Nguesso returned home on Sunday after 17 months in France to an enthusiastic welcome from thousands of supporters who want him to run for president.

Witnesses said more than 10,000 militants of his former single party, the Congolese Labour Party (PCT), turned out to welcome him at Brazzaville international airport and that crowds cheered him on the way to his northern Brazzaville stronghold.

Sassou-Nguesso, who trailed President Pascal Lissouba and Lissouba's civilian rival Bernard Kolelas in the 1992 presidential election, said he had returned to follow closely preparations for the next presidential poll scheduled for July.
"I will examine the question with officials of my party," he told reporters, when asked whether he planned to stand.
Sassou-Nguesso, who describes his stay in France as private, threw his weight behind calls for an independent national electoral commission, a demand rejected by Prime Minister Charles David Ganao.
Fighting among politically and ethnically-based militias loyal to Congo's political rivals after disputed elections in 1993 killed an estimated 2,000 people in Brazzaville's suburbs.
The militias have officially disbanded but witnesses say their members remain ever present, albeit discreetly. Sassou-Nguesso's militia was called the Cobras.
Military sources said this week that about 50 officers from his Mbochi tribe had decided to back his candidacy. The 1992 constitution bans serving soldiers from political activity.
